FIFO scheduling is a first-in-first-out algorithm that processes jobs based on their arrival order. It ensures that the oldest job in the queue is executed immediately, guaranteeing fair treatment for all arriving processes regardless of their relative timing. This simple rule creates a predictable and stable system where the earliest entry is always served first.

The core operation involves maintaining a queue where the head of the line holds the most recent job. When a process arrives, it is added to the front of this queue, and the oldest job is removed and executed next. This structure prevents any single job from dominating the system by ensuring no process blocks others indefinitely.

A practical example involves a server managing a batch of incoming files. If a new file arrives at 10:00 AM, it is placed at the head of the queue. The oldest file, 10:00 AM, is processed first, while the newest file, 10:05 AM, waits until 10:05. This method ensures that the most recent activity is handled before the oldest, maintaining system efficiency.

The primary advantage of FIFO is its simplicity and fairness. Unlike priority-based systems where a high-priority job might block others, FIFO treats all jobs equally based on their entry time. This prevents any single process from monopolizing resources, ensuring that all users receive their share of the system's capacity.

Head-of-line blocking occurs when a process waiting in the queue cannot proceed because the oldest job is already being executed. This happens when the system is overloaded or when a new job arrives faster than the oldest one. In such cases, the system may delay the head-of-line job until the queue empties, which can cause delays for waiting processes.

Compared to other policies, FIFO is generally preferred for its simplicity and lack of complexity. It is often used in real-time systems where strict timing is critical, such as in manufacturing or emergency response scenarios. While other policies like Round Robin might offer better fairness, FIFO remains the standard for its reliability and predictable behavior.

END
